steps.say: Short bowel syndrome is defined by what remains after surgery, not by what was removed. A child with less than a quarter of expected small bowel for age, or under thirty to fifty centimetres without a valve, faces intestinal failure. Losing the ileocecal valve lowers the limit to fifteen to twenty centimetres, because the valve slows transit and guards the small bowel. Measure the remnant at operation and write the number down.
steps.tx: The **anatomical definition of SBS** in children rests on remnant length, not on the disease that removed it. Short bowel syndrome follows resection leaving under **25%** of expected small bowel for gestational age, under **30-50 cm** without an ileocecal valve, or under **15-20 cm** when the **valve** is preserved. The operating surgeon must measure and record the remnant, since that number predicts years of parenteral nutrition.

steps.say: Necrotising enterocolitis fills more short bowel beds than any other disease. Roughly thirty five to forty percent of paediatric intestinal failure starts with NEC in a premature baby, followed by atresias, midgut volvulus, and gastroschisis. Each condition strikes the newborn gut before it has grown reserve. Preventing NEC through breast milk and cautious feeding advances would shrink this whole population.
steps.tx: The **etiology in neonates** is led overwhelmingly by necrotising enterocolitis. **NEC** causes **35-40%** of paediatric intestinal failure, with intestinal **atresia**, midgut **volvulus**, and **gastroschisis** covering most of the rest. Every one of these strikes before the gut has grown reserve, which is why neonatal surgical units, not adult wards, carry this burden.

vis.alt: Neonatal abdominal radiograph showing pneumatosis intestinalis with branching lucencies in the liver and dilated bowel loops of necrotising enterocolitis.
vis.caption: Pneumatosis and dilated loops mark necrotising enterocolitis, the leading cause of short bowel syndrome. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Saving the ileocecal valve at resection changes the whole prognosis. The valve brakes the flow of chyme so food lingers against absorbing mucosa, effectively doubling fluid uptake. It also bars colonic bacteria from marching back into the small bowel, where they would compete for nutrients and deconjugate bile acids. A surgeon who preserves even a battered valve gives adaptation its best chance.
steps.tx: The **role of the ileocecal valve** explains why centimetres alone never tell the story. A preserved valve slows transit so mucosal contact time doubles fluid absorption, and it blocks retrograde **bacterial colonisation** from the colon into the small bowel. Resections that sacrifice the valve trade faster transit for bacterial overgrowth, so every operative note must state the valve status plainly.

points: Bars colonic bacteria from small bowel
Keeps bile acids conjugated for fat uptake
left.title: Valve preserved

steps.say: Jejunum and ileum do not adapt equally, and the difference guides prognosis. The ileum alone can grow taller villi and deeper crypts after resection, expanding its surface over months. It also owns the only receptors for vitamin B12 and conjugated bile acids, so an ileal remnant protects against two classic deficiencies. A pure jejunal remnant, however long, can never reclaim those jobs.
steps.tx: **Ileum vs jejunum adaptation** decides which remnants can wean off drips. Only the **ileum** grows mucosal hyperplasia with taller villi and deeper crypts, steadily expanding surface area, and only it carries receptors for **vitamin B12** and conjugated **bile acids**. A jejunal remnant keeps digesting but cannot reclaim those two absorptive jobs, so ileal preservation outranks raw length.

steps.say: Liver disease stalks every child on long term parenteral nutrition. Cholestasis builds when the gut sees no food, soybean lipid runs continuously, phytosterols accumulate, and line infections recur. Bilirubin climbs while feeds still run through a vein, and the slide can be silent until fibrosis is advanced. Prevention starts on day one with any trickle of enteral feed the remnant tolerates.
steps.tx: **Intestinal failure-associated liver disease**, or IFALD, is the shadow over long term parenteral nutrition. Cholestasis follows absent **enteral stimulation**, continuous intravenous **soybean lipid** emulsions with **phytosterols**, and recurrent central line **sepsis**. Bilirubin rises while calories still arrive by vein, so teams track liver tests weekly and push even tiny enteral trickles to keep bile flowing.

vis.alt: Diagram of central venous catheter infection with erythema and purulence at the insertion site and paired blood culture sampling.
vis.caption: Line infection at the catheter site is a constant threat during long term parenteral nutrition. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Fish oil emulsions rescued livers that soybean oil was destroying. Swapping pure soybean lipid for a fish oil based emulsion such as Omegaven reverses cholestasis in many infants, because omega 3 fatty acids calm inflammation and alpha tocopherol shields hepatocytes. Bilirubin often falls within weeks of the switch. Modern units now start mixed or fish based lipids before jaundice ever appears.
steps.tx: **Fish-oil lipid rescue** reverses cholestasis where soybean emulsions caused it. Substituting pure soybean lipid with fish oil based emulsion (**Omegaven**) clears jaundice through high **omega-3 fatty acids** plus protective **alpha-tocopherol**. Units that switch early watch bilirubin fall within weeks, and many now begin mixed lipids prophylactically so IFALD never gathers pace.

nodes.label: Switch to fish oil based Omegaven
Protect the liver, push enteral feeds

steps.say: Teduglutide gives the remnant gut a pharmacological growth signal. This recombinant glucagon like peptide 2 analogue drives crypt cell proliferation and villus hypertrophy, thickening the very mucosa that absorbs. Parenteral volume requirements fall as absorption climbs, and some children cut infusion days each week. It complements, never replaces, the slow work of enteral advancement and hygiene.
steps.tx: The **teduglutide GLP-2 analogue** is the first drug that grows bowel rather than resting it. Recombinant human **glucagon-like peptide-2** stimulates crypt proliferation and **villus hypertrophy**, expanding absorptive surface in the remnant. Parenteral nutrition volumes fall as enteral tolerance climbs, and regulators approved it for children after trials showed fewer infusion hours per week.

steps.say: Dilated floppy loops are dead space, and lengthening operations recruit them back. Serial transverse enteroplasty staples the dilated bowel into a zigzag channel, while the Bianchi longitudinal procedure splits one wide loop into two narrow parallel limbs. Both expand mucosal surface without sacrificing a centimetre of length. Timing matters: operate once dilation is clear but before liver failure closes the window.
steps.tx: **Surgical lengthening procedures** reclaim dilated bowel that has stopped propelling. **Serial Transverse Enteroplasty** (STEP) staples a wide loop into a zigzag channel, and **Longitudinal Intestinal Lengthening and Tailoring** (LILT, Bianchi) splits one dilated segment into two narrow limbs. Both add absorptive surface with zero length lost, and both work best after the remnant dilates but before advanced liver disease.

points: Splits one loop into two limbs
right.title: LILT Bianchi procedure
